attempts.summary: Established an AIDE-based file-integrity baseline for /etc on node1 (Ubuntu 16.04). Installed aide/aide-common, verified the packaged Debian/Ubuntu AIDE config recursively applies full content checksums (SHA256/SHA512/RMD160/TIGER/HAVAL/GOST/CRC32 + metadata) to /etc via the "/ Full" catch-all rule (with narrow, pre-existing exceptions for known-volatile files like resolv.conf/adjtime), initialized the baseline database at /var/lib/aide/aide.db (70,149 entries), and proved detection works end-to-end by tampering with /etc/hosts, running aide --check, observing the exact checksum/size/mtime diff reported, then restoring /etc/hosts and re-baselining to a clean state. The distro's /etc/cron.daily/aide job (already enabled) will run these checks automatically going forward and report changes. Completed the mandatory restart-evidence protocol on node1: captured pre-restart boot_id and a clean /etc AIDE check, issued a background `reboot` so the ack returned before disconnect, polled until exec access returned, confirmed boot_id changed (a1dc8e25... -> 2e616fe5...), and confirmed post-restart that the AIDE database file was intact (same md5) and a fresh aide --check showed zero differences under real /etc paths (all reported diffs were in /run, lxcfs cgroup pseudo-files from ephemeral SSH sessions, or postfix's chroot copies under /var/spool/postfix/etc, none in /etc itself).
